question.problem: Let $A(-2, 4, -2, 2)$ and $B(4, 0, -1, -4).$ Find the cosine of the angle $\angle{AOB},$ where $O(0,0,0,0)$ is the origin.
question.worked_solution:
First, let

$$
\begin{aligned}a=\overset{\to }{OA}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,b=\overset{\to }{OB}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Also, let $\theta = m\angle{AOB}$ be the angle between the vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}.$ Then, we can find $\cos \theta$ using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{‖a‖\,‖b‖} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{1}{b}_{1}+{a}_{2}{b}_{2}+{a}_{3}{b}_{3}+{a}_{4}{b}_{4}}{\sqrt{{a}_{1}^{2}+{a}_{2}^{2}+{a}_{3}^{2}+{a}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{b}_{1}^{2}+{b}_{2}^{2}+{b}_{3}^{2}+{b}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{(-2)\cdot 4+4\cdot 0+(-2)\cdot (-1)+2\cdot (-4)}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{4}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-4)^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{-14}{\sqrt{28}\cdot \sqrt{33}} \\  & =\frac{-14}{\sqrt{14}\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{33}} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{14}}{\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{33}} \\  & =-\sqrt{\frac{7}{33}}\end{aligned}
$$
